name: gizza-ai/csr-generator
summary: Generate an ECDSA private key and PKCS#10 CSR

tool.description: Generate a fresh ECDSA private key and PKCS#10 Certificate Signing Request (CSR) locally. Choose p256 (default) or p384, fill subject fields (CN plus optional O/OU/C/ST/L), and add DNS, IP, email, or URI Subject Alternative Names. The output includes PKCS#8 private key PEM, public key PEM, CSR PEM, and a subject/SAN summary. RSA is listed as out-of-model for this wasm-safe RustCrypto implementation; use an external OpenSSL flow if a CA specifically requires RSA.

algorithm.description: ECDSA signing key for the CSR: p256 (secp256r1, broad TLS support, default) or p384 (larger curve, SHA-384 signature). RSA CSR generation is intentionally not exposed in this wasm-safe RustCrypto implementation.

common_name.description: Subject common name (CN), usually the primary DNS name such as example.com. If no SANs are supplied and this looks like a DNS name, it is also added as a DNS SAN.

country.description: Optional two-letter subject country code (C), for example US or GB.

locality.description: Optional subject locality/city (L), for example San Francisco.

organization.description: Optional subject organization (O), for example Example Ltd.

organizational_unit.description: Optional subject organizational unit (OU), for example Platform or IT.

san_dns.description: Optional DNS Subject Alternative Names, separated by commas, semicolons, or new lines. Prefixes like DNS:api.example.com are accepted.

san_emails.description: Optional email/rfc822Name Subject Alternative Names, separated by commas, semicolons, or new lines. email: prefixes are optional.

san_ips.description: Optional IP address Subject Alternative Names, separated by commas, semicolons, or new lines. IPv4 and IPv6 are accepted; IP: prefixes are optional.

san_uris.description: Optional URI Subject Alternative Names, separated by commas, semicolons, or new lines. URI: prefixes are optional.

state.description: Optional subject state or province (ST), for example California.
